Without a strong feedback culture, however, teams often fall into stagnation, misalignment, and quiet frustration. Problems go unspoken, growth stalls, and trust can quietly erode. Over time, the lack of honest conversations becomes a bigger blocker than any technical debt.

然而，没有强大的反馈文化，团队往往会陷入停滞、对齐失灵和无声的挫败。问题无人提及，成长陷入停顿，信任也可能悄悄流失。久而久之，缺乏坦诚对话会变成比任何技术债都更大的拦路虎。

— PDF p.149 —

But even being aware of all its benefits, many developers aren't fans of feedback because it can feel uncomfortable and might even put them in a tricky situation with another team member. Also, proper feedback requires preparation and time that they just prefer putting into something else.

但即便清楚它的种种好处，许多开发并不喜欢反馈这件事——因为它让人不自在，甚至可能让他们在和另一位团队成员相处时陷入尴尬。而且，像样的反馈需要准备和时间，而他们更愿意把这些投到别的事情上。

The strategies in this chapter will help your team feel more comfortable giving you feedback and make that feedback more useful and actionable. But if you want to build a true feedback culture, that's not enough. A strong team culture requires everyone to be involved: you don't want feedback flowing only between you and your team members but also among the team members themselves.

本章中的那些策略，会帮你的团队更自在地给你反馈，并让这些反馈更有用、更可落地。但如果你想建立真正的反馈文化，光有这些还不够。一支强大的团队文化，需要每个人都参与进来：你要的不只是在你和成员之间流动的反馈，更是在成员彼此之间流动的反馈。

Here are some strategies that can help you to have this multiplying effect:

下面这些策略，能帮你实现这种"放大效应"：

Start with you从你自己开始

One of the most powerful tools you have to shape your team's culture, especially around feedback, is leading by example. It's not just about telling people what to do but about showing them every single day. Consistency is key here. How you handle feedback, the priority you give it, and the effort you invest all set the standard for what you expect from others.

在塑造团队文化——尤其是反馈文化——方面，你最有力的工具之一就是以身作则。它不只是告诉别人该做什么，而是每一天都做给他们看。在这里，一致性是关键。你如何对待反馈、你赋予它多高的优先级、你为此投入多少心力，都在为你对他人的期待立下标准。

If you want your team to embrace feedback, start with how you approach it. Show them what asking for feedback looks like, how to receive it gracefully, and what to do with it afterward. Apply the same care and effort when you give feedback, whether it's positive or constructive.

如果你希望团队拥抱反馈，就从你自己如何对待它开始。向他们展示：请求反馈是什么样子、如何优雅地接收它、以及收到之后该怎么处理。你给出反馈时——无论是正面的还是建设性的——也要投入同样的用心和精力。

Let your team see how you incorporate feedback. Share examples of when a piece of feedback led you to change something, whether it's how you run a meeting, communicate an idea, or manage a process, and what happened as a result.

让团队看到你是如何把反馈消化吸收的。分享一些例子：某条反馈曾让你做出改变——无论是改变你主持会议的方式、沟通想法的方式，还是管理流程的方式——以及后来结果如何。

Build psychological safety建立心理安全

For your team to consistently provide honest feedback, they must feel psychologically safe. This means creating an environment where they feel comfortable speaking up, sharing ideas, and expressing their thoughts without fear of negative consequences. They need to trust that their input won't harm their chances of promotion or damage relationships within the team.

要让团队持续给出诚实的反馈，他们必须在心理上感到安全。这意味着营造一个环境，让他们敢于开口、分享想法、表达观点，而不必担心负面后果。他们需要相信：自己的意见不会损害晋升的机会，也不会破坏团队内部的关系。

Psychological safety is the foundation for open communication, and without it, feedback will always be limited or surface-level. I'll dive deeper into this critical topic in the section "How to Create Psychological Safety on Your Team" on page 188, but it's worth remembering that trust and safety take time and consistent effort to build.

心理安全是开放沟通的基石；没有它，反馈永远会受限、或停留在表面。我会在第 188 页"如何在团队中建立心理安全"一节里深入探讨这个关键话题，但这里值得先记住：信任与安全，需要时间和持续的努力才能建立起来。

— PDF p.150 —

Encourage feedback between team members鼓励成员之间互相反馈

Feedback shouldn't flow only between you and your team members; it needs to happen among them too. For example, when two team members are in conflict and one comes to you frustrated, don't take on the problem as your own. Instead, encourage them to provide direct feedback to the other person. Help them prepare for the conversation by walking through what they want to say and how they might say it. Remind them to focus on the behavior and its impact, not on judging the person. You can even rehearse the conversation together and help them rephrase statements using the same principles we've covered earlier: be specific, clear, and honest, and avoid assumptions.

反馈不该只在你和成员之间流动；它也需要在成员彼此之间发生。例如，当两位成员起了冲突、其中一方带着委屈来找你时，不要把问题揽到自己身上。相反，鼓励他直接向对方反馈。帮他准备这场谈话：一起过一遍他想说什么、可以怎么说。提醒他聚焦行为及其影响，而不是评判这个人。你们甚至可以一起预演这场对话，并用我们前面讲过的原则帮他把措辞改一改：要具体、清晰、诚实，并避免臆断。

Educate your team on feedback教会团队如何反馈

Your team may not naturally know how to give or receive feedback. Teach them what useful feedback looks like and share strategies to make it more effective. Demonstrate the importance of being specific, clear, and honest. Explain how feedback can help the team grow and improve, not just individually but collectively. You can do all this in an open session with your team about feedback.

你的团队未必天生就懂得如何给出或接收反馈。教他们：有用的反馈长什么样、并分享让它更有效的策略。示范"具体、清晰、诚实"的重要性。解释反馈如何帮助团队成长与进步——不仅是个人层面，更是集体层面。这一切，你都可以在一次和团队一起、关于反馈的开放讨论中完成。

Create opportunities to practice feedback创造练习反馈的机会

A great way to introduce this practice is through an exercise called Speedback. Speedback is a quick, structured way for teams to practice feedback. I first encountered it during my time at Thoughtworks, and I've used it in every team since.

引入这种练习的一个好办法，是通过一个叫"Speedback"的活动。Speedback 是一种让团队快速、结构化地练习反馈的方式。我最早是在 Thoughtworks 时接触到它的，此后每一支团队我都用过。

Speedback is a simple and efficient method for exchanging feedback among team members. The process involves pairing team members for four minutes, during which each person has two minutes to give feedback to their partner. After the four minutes, the pairs rotate, and the process repeats until everyone has had the chance to exchange feedback with every other team member. This can be done either face-to-face or remotely using tools like Zoom breakout rooms.

Speedback 是一种在成员之间交换反馈的简单高效的方法。流程是：把成员两两配对，进行四分钟，在这四分钟里每人有两分钟向搭档给出反馈。四分钟后，配对轮换，流程重复，直到每个人都和其他所有成员交换过反馈。这既可以面对面进行，也可以借助 Zoom 分组会议室之类的工具远程开展。

To ensure the session runs smoothly, block time on everyone's calendar in advance, including 30 minutes of dedicated preparation time for them to put together the feedback, and share tips for giving useful feedback to set expectations. A straightforward structure works best: for example, team members can share two things the other person should continue doing and two areas for improvement. Or it can be as simple as one thing: "One thing I appreciate about working with you is…" and "One area where I think you could grow is…" If possible, involve an external facilitator to handle the logistics, such as tracking time and managing transitions, so participants can focus entirely on the feedback exchange.

为了让活动顺利进行，提前在每个人的日历上留出时间，其中包括 30 分钟专门的准备时间，让他们把反馈整理好；并分享给出有用反馈的技巧、以设定预期。一个简单直接的结构效果最好：例如，成员可以分享"对方应该继续保持的两件事"和"两个可改进的方面"。或者可以简单到只说一件事："和你合作，我很欣赏的一点是……"以及"我觉得你可以成长的一个方面是……"如果可能，请一位外部引导者来处理后勤——比如计时和轮换——这样参与者就能全身心投入到反馈交流中。

— PDF p.151 —

It's important to emphasize that Speedback is just the starting point for deeper conversations. The goal is to trigger follow-up discussions where participants can explore the feedback further, share examples, and define actionable steps. These sessions are particularly useful after completing a significant milestone, when joining a new team, or during periods of complicated team dynamics, but I advise you to run them monthly just to get into the habit.

要强调的是：Speedback 只是开启更深入对话的起点。它的目标，是引发后续的讨论，让参与者可以进一步探讨反馈、分享例子、并定义可落地的步骤。这种活动在完成一个重要里程碑之后、加入新团队时、或团队关系错综复杂的时期尤其有用；但我建议你干脆每月都办一次，好养成习惯。

Make feedback a constant process让反馈成为持续的过程

As useful as Speedback sessions are to get your team started with feedback, they are not a replacement for ongoing feedback. Running one session a month doesn't mean you've established a feedback culture in your team. To embed feedback into your team's culture, it needs to happen consistently and naturally as part of your team's ways of working. Start by planning regular Speedback sessions to get everyone comfortable with giving and receiving feedback. But don't stop there. Follow up with broader conversations and encourage the team to keep those discussions alive.

尽管 Speedback 活动能帮团队入门反馈，但它并不能取代日常持续的反馈。每月办一次活动，并不意味着你就在团队里建立起了反馈文化。要把反馈嵌入团队的文化，它必须持续而自然地发生，成为团队工作方式的一部分。先通过安排定期的 Speedback，让大家习惯给出和接收反馈。但不要止步于此。再跟进更广泛的对话，并鼓励团队让这些讨论持续下去。

Involve your team in sustaining this process. Ask for volunteers to help move the initiative forward, whether it's planning the sessions, tracking progress, or scheduling time on everyone's calendar. When the effort doesn't just come from you but also from other team members, people are often more receptive. It also signals that feedback is a shared responsibility, not just something pushed by leadership.

让团队一起参与维系这个过程。请志愿者来帮忙推动这件事——无论是策划活动、跟踪进展，还是在每个人的日历上排时间。当这份努力不只来自你、也来自其他成员时，大家往往更愿意接受。这也传递出一个信号：反馈是大家共同的责任，而不只是领导层在推的一件事。

If you notice that feedback isn't happening as often as it should, address it in your team retrospectives. Reflecting on how feedback is exchanged is just as relevant and valuable a topic for a retrospective as discussing how a feature was delivered, since strong feedback practices directly impact collaboration, alignment, and, ultimately, delivery outcomes.

如果你注意到反馈发生的频率不够，就在团队复盘里把它提出来。反思"反馈是如何交换的"，和讨论"某个功能是怎么交付的"一样，都是复盘里既切题又有价值的话题——因为良好的反馈实践会直接影响协作、对齐，并最终影响交付结果。

Track progress跟踪进展

Like any process, tracking and measuring the success of your feedback efforts is essential. How else will you know you are improving? Start small with metrics like the number of feedback sessions held, how many people are actively involved, and how ownership is being shared. Beyond the numbers, focus on the impact feedback is having on your team.

和任何流程一样，跟踪并衡量你在反馈上所做努力是否成功，至关重要。否则你怎么知道自己在进步？先用一些小指标起步：举办了多少次反馈活动、有多少人积极参与、以及主人翁感是如何被分担的。在数字之外，更要关注反馈给团队带来的影响。

— PDF p.152 —

Ask yourself: "Are people acting on the feedback they receive, or is it being ignored?" or "Are your efforts making feedback a visible and valued part of your team?"

问问你自己："人们有把收到的反馈付诸行动吗，还是被置之不理？"或者"你的努力，有没有让反馈成为团队中一个看得见、受重视的部分？"

Look for signs that things are improving. For instance, team members might feel less stressed and more prepared during performance reviews because they've already received regular feedback throughout the year. This reduces the pressure of last-minute feedback prep and ensures there are no big surprises.

留意那些表明情况在好转的迹象。例如，团队成员在绩效评估时可能压力更小、准备更充分，因为他们一整年里已经持续收到反馈了。这减轻了"临阵磨枪准备反馈"的压力，也确保不会出现大的意外。

Different stages of your team's development might require different ways to measure success. The key is to focus on what works best for your team right now and adapt as you go.

团队发展的不同阶段，可能需要用不同的方式来衡量成功。关键在于：聚焦于当下最适合你团队的方式，并随进程不断调整。

Building a feedback culture requires a mindset shift and an ongoing commitment. The real payoff comes when feedback becomes second nature: when your team regularly gives and receives feedback, reflects on it, and acts on it without prompting. That's when feedback stops being a "thing you do" and becomes just part of how your team works and grows together.

建立反馈文化，需要一次心态上的转变和一份持续的投入。真正的回报，出现在反馈变成第二天性的时候：当你的团队会主动地、定期地给出和接收反馈、反思它、并据此行动。到那时，反馈就不再是"你要去做的一件事"，而成为你们团队协作与共同成长方式的一部分。

Start small, be consistent, and keep showing up for the process. Over time, the ripple effects will show, in your team's collaboration, growth, and ability to tackle challenges.

从小处起步，保持一贯，并持续投入这个过程。久而久之，涟漪效应就会显现——在团队的协作、成长，以及攻坚克难的能力上。

Key Takeaway本章要点

Feedback is how teams grow…and it starts with you.

反馈，是团队成长之道……而它，始于你。

Creating a feedback culture means making feedback a natural, expected, and valued part of your team's daily rhythm. That includes asking for feedback regularly, receiving it with humility, giving it clearly and consistently, and creating space for others to do the same, not just with you but with each other.

营造反馈文化，意味着让反馈成为团队日常节奏中自然发生、理所当然、并被珍视的一部分。这包括：定期请求反馈、以谦逊之心接收反馈、清晰而持续地给出反馈，并为他人——不只是对你、也包括彼此之间——创造同样去做的空间。

It takes practice, courage, and care. But when done well, feedback strengthens relationships, accelerates growth, and builds a foundation of trust that will carry your team through every challenge.

这需要练习、勇气和用心。但只要做得好，反馈就能巩固关系、加速成长，并打下一份信任的根基，托着你的团队闯过每一个挑战。

You won't get it right every time, and that's OK. Just stay open, stay human, and keep the conversation going.

你不可能每次都做得完美，而这没关系。只要保持开放、保持真诚，并让对话一直延续下去就好。
